question: A 30-year-old woman, G3P2, has just delivered vaginally at 38 weeks. The placenta is expelled but estimated blood loss is 700 mL and continues. BP is 90/60 mmHg, PR 118/min. Which uterotonic is CONTRAINDICATED for managing this postpartum haemorrhage?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Oxytocin 10 IU IM is the WHO-recommended first-line uterotonic for PPH management. It is safe and is not contraindicated in this setting.

Correct. Ergometrine is contraindicated in hypertensive disorders, including pre-eclampsia and any woman with elevated blood pressure. It causes intense vasoconstriction and can precipitate hypertensive crisis, stroke, or myocardial infarction. Always check BP before using ergometrine.
Incorrect. Misoprostol is an effective uterotonic used in PPH management when oxytocin is unavailable or insufficient; it is not contraindicated in this scenario.
Incorrect. Tranexamic acid is recommended within 3 hours of PPH onset to reduce mortality; it is not a uterotonic but is a safe adjunct and is not contraindicated here.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember the PPH uterotonic contraindication: ergometrine is contraindicated when BP is elevated (hypertension, pre-eclampsia). Although BP here is low from haemorrhage, ergometrine's vasoconstriction risk makes oxytocin and misoprostol safer choices.
Correct. Ergometrine is contraindicated in hypertension (including pre-eclampsia, eclampsia, and any elevated BP). This is one of the highest-yield PPH contraindication traps in OG examinations.
